correctness.rationale: For odd circumference a rung must occur, forcing horizontal edges to form matched pairs. The absent rung at column zero forces precisely two neighboring horizontal pairs, partitioning perfect-matching facets. Both generated complexes are cones; their face-wise overlap is exactly the perfect-matching complex of the induced 2-by-(n-3) strip, by restriction and extension in both directions. The strip has an independent two-cone suspension recurrence based on two disjoint facets for length two. Cofibration gluing gives an integral sphere. Explicit boundary reductions in nine finite instances corroborate the proof; they are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural minimal perturbation of a graph family classified in a current paper changes its perfect-matching complex from contractible to a single sphere in unbounded dimension. The family and dimension dependence are structural rather than a small finite census. The exact cone intersection also explains the transition and gives a uniform constructive homotopy argument.
